newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: ANZ says bank criticism unfair.
newsitem.headline: ANZ says bank criticism unfair.

text.p: Australia and New Zealand Banking Group Ltd, one of Australia's four biggest banks, on Wednesday hit back at recent criticism by politicians of Australia's big banks, describing it as "irresponsible and unfair."
ANZ chief executive Don Mercer told a news conference the major banks had been unfairly accused of not passing on official interest rate cuts to customers.
He said the banks had collectively cut variable mortgage rates by 330 basis points since the middle of last year while official rates had been cut by only 200 basis points.
"We have passed on more than the reductions in the cash rate," Mercer told a news conference announcing a 24 percent rise in first half profits. "It really isn't fair," he said.
Mercer said he was "very, very disappointed with this bank bashing."

The four major banks cut their variable mortgage rates by 35 basis points on Friday after the Reserve Bank's 50 basis point cut in official interest rates, sparking a round of criticism from politicians and consumer groups who claimed the banks had taken the opportunity to bolster their profits.
ANZ has subsequently cut its variable mortgage rate again, in effect reducing its rate by 56 basis points to 6.99 percent since the official rate cut.

Ironically, Mercer's comments came after Treasurer Peter Costello, who had attacked the banks sharply in the last week, praised the ANZ for passing on all of Friday's rate cut and recommended consumers bank with those like the ANZ, St George Bank and Aussie Home loans who had passed it all on.
"The ANZ is now the most competitive bank on home rates of the majors," Costello said in a Melbourne radio earlier on Wednesday.
Costello went on to attack those major banks that had not passed on all the cut.
"The rate cuts were for consumers. That cut (on Friday) was not done for the benefit of the banks," Costello said.
"It wasn't done so that the banks could do a bit of price taking along the way."
Meanwhile Mercer said banks had become easy targets for politicians aiming to garner further political support.
"We're a free kick. Any time a politician wants a free kick, they just bash the banks. You can't lose," Mercer said.
